verdict.evidence: Repro output (jsdom, the actual test env, with standards-compliant KeyboardEvent): `[fact] real-browser Shift+Z key="Z" shiftKey=true` / `[fact] unit-test artificial key="z" shiftKey=true` / `[real macOS] Cmd+Shift+Z(key="Z") -> action=null prevented=false` then `AssertionError: BUG REPRODUCED: real-browser Cmd+Shift+Z dispatched action=null (expected "redo")`. Code-trace of frontend/src/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts: line 54 `if (mod && e.key === "z" && e.shiftKey && !isTyping)` — when shiftKey is held the browser sets e.key to uppercase "Z", so `e.key === "z" && e.shiftKey` is never simultaneously true (confirmed: jsdom stores "Z" verbatim and the line-54 predicate evaluates false). Line 49 undo `e.key === "z" && !e.shiftKey` works because Ctrl/Cmd alone does not change case. Line 60 redo `e.key === "y"` is Ctrl+Y (Windows only); there is no Cmd+Y on macOS, so Mac keyboard redo is entirely dead. Grep confirmed no `.toLowerCase()`/`e.code`/`KeyZ` normalization anywhere and no other redo key binding. The existing test (useKeyboardShortcuts.test.ts:67-70) fires `fireKey("z", {ctrlKey:true, shiftKey:true})` — an artificial key:"z"+shift combo no real browser emits — which my repro shows reaches redo (false green), masking the breakage.
verdict.recommended_fix: Make the letter comparisons case-insensitive on the undo/redo branches: replace `e.key === "z"` with `e.key.toLowerCase() === "z"` at lines 49 and 54 (the undo branch already gates on `!e.shiftKey`, so lowercasing is safe). This lets Shift+Z ("Z") match line 54 and restores Ctrl+Shift+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z redo on all platforms. Add a regression test that fires the realistic event `fireKey("Z", { metaKey: true, shiftKey: true })` (uppercase key, the value real browsers emit) and asserts redo is called; the artificial key:"z"+shift test should be corrected/removed since it cannot occur in a browser. Optionally lowercase the other single-letter shortcuts (s/y/c/v/a/k/g) for Caps-Lock robustness, lower priority. Note the Toolbar Redo button (aria-label="Redo", title="Redo (Ctrl+Shift+Z)") still works via mouse, so redo is not wholly lost — but the advertised keyboard accelerator is dead, which is why this is a genuine medium-severity user-facing logic bug rather than a cosmetic one.
